findings.text: The first lede tells a newcomer what Athena is and what sets it apart in two sentences. That is a strong opening.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost."

findings.text: Everything below the header is about firstmate, a different project. That leaves three sentences about Athena on Athena's own site. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena gets a long sample of its output but little about how Athena works or how it made this study.
findings.source: "This page is that study of firstmate." / title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The next step is linked from the header, and the Next steps section gives a repository link and an example command. A newcomer can find what to do next quickly.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself"

findings.text: The install step assumes the reader already has a checkout. It gives no clone command and lists no prerequisites, such as a Rust toolchain or AI model API keys, so 'athena ask' may not work on the first try.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh"

findings.text: The section labelled 'Start here' quickly moves into exit codes, locks, durable records and fast-forwards. A newcomer meets implementation detail before having a clear picture, which makes the page harder to read than it needs to be.
findings.source: Start here, "When things go wrong": "the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued"; "lands the ready branch by a guarded fast-forward"

findings.text: The page is honest about what its sources do not say, which builds trust. But some entries define a term only by saying it is undefined, and several definitions appear word for word twice ('in scope', 'red', 'home'). This adds length without adding clarity.
findings.source: Words used first: "in scope ... The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."

findings.text: Every sentence links to a claim, and every claim links to exact file lines at a pinned commit. This makes the 'why it matters' point concrete, though the citation markers on every line make the page tiring to scan.
findings.source: "Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end."

findings.text: The page says plainly that firstmate's code was read but never run. This helps a newcomer judge how much to trust the study.
findings.source: Limits of this study: "f1 not run ... no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read."

findings.text: This refers to a repository folder the newcomer has not seen and gives no link, so it means little to them.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
